name: browser_automation
description: Drive a real headless Chromium browser: open pages, read the rendered text and HTML, click, type into and submit forms, run JavaScript, follow links, scroll, take screenshots, and export the page as a PDF. Use it for JavaScript-rendered sites, multi-step flows and forms — anything a plain HTTP fetch cannot do. State is kept in a browsing session so a sequence of steps shares cookies and the current page.
usecases: you need to read a page that only renders its content with JavaScript (a plain fetch returns an empty shell)
you need to interact with a site: click buttons, fill and submit a form, log in, step through a flow
you need a screenshot of a page (or an element), or the page exported as a PDF
you need to run JavaScript in the page and read the result, or extract data after the page settles
you need to follow a multi-step navigation while keeping cookies/session between steps
howToTalk: Signal it with `function` naming the operation. Start with `navigate` (`url`). Then read with `text` (rendered text, optional `selector`), `content` (HTML), `links`, or `screenshot` (returns base64 `image`; `format`=jpeg|png, `full_page`, `selector`). Interact with `click` (`selector`), `fill`/`type` (`selector`+`text`, optional `enter`), `press` (`key`), `scroll` (`to`=top|bottom or `dy`), `evaluate` (`script` = a JS expression). Navigation: `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `wait_for` (`selector` or `wait_until`), `set_viewport`. `current` reports the URL+title; `sessions` lists open sessions; `close` ends one. All steps in one space share a session (its own cookies and current page); pass `session` for a second parallel tab.
prompt: Use this to drive a real browser when a plain web fetch is not enough — JS-rendered pages, logins, forms, multi-step flows, screenshots. `navigate` to a URL, then `text`/`content`/`links`/`screenshot` to read it and `click`/`fill`/`press`/`evaluate` to interact. Steps share a browsing session (cookies + current page) so you can log in once and keep going. Selectors are CSS (or Playwright text= selectors). Screenshots come back as base64.

function.description: operation: navigate (default) | text | content | links | screenshot | click | fill | type | press | evaluate | scroll | wait_for | back | forward | reload | set_viewport | current | pdf | sessions | close

url.description: for navigate: the page URL to open

text.description: for fill/type: the text to enter into the selected field

key.description: for press: a key or chord, e.g. "Enter", "Control+A"

script.description: for evaluate: a JavaScript expression to run in the page

full_page.description: for screenshot: capture the whole scrollable page

enter.description: for fill: press Enter after typing (submit)

to.description: for scroll: top | bottom (or use dy for a pixel delta)

session.description: name a parallel browsing session (tab); default is one shared session

tools.name: navigate
tools.desc: open a URL in the session's page and wait for it to load; the usual first step

tools.name: text
tools.desc: return the rendered (visible) text of the page or a selected element

tools.name: content
tools.desc: return the page's current HTML (after JavaScript has run)

tools.name: links
tools.desc: list the page's outbound links as {text, url}

tools.name: screenshot
tools.desc: capture the page (or an element) and return a base64 image

selector.desc: optional element to capture instead of the viewport

tools.name: click
tools.desc: click the element matching a selector

selector.desc: CSS or text= selector to click

tools.name: fill
tools.desc: type text into an input/textarea (optionally pressing Enter to submit)

tools.name: press
tools.desc: press a keyboard key or chord (on a selector, or the focused element)

tools.name: evaluate
tools.desc: run a JavaScript expression in the page and return its result

tools.name: scroll
tools.desc: scroll the page (to top/bottom, or by a pixel delta)

tools.name: wait_for
tools.desc: wait for a selector to appear (or a load state / a fixed delay)

tools.name: current
tools.desc: report the session's current URL and title

tools.name: pdf
tools.desc: render the current page to a PDF and return it as base64

tools.name: close
tools.desc: close a browsing session (frees the browser context)

session.desc: the session name (default: the shared one)
